title: Auth-token burst triggered gateway thundering-herd and partial quota accounting collapse
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a customer-facing load spike on 2026-03-05 an expired-authentication token refresh pattern from several mobile clients caused hundreds of concurrent reauthenticate calls. The gateway's quota accounting and routing pipeline failed to apply backpressure in time, resulting in cascading downstream overloads and elevated 503s for a 17-minute window. Key symptoms: sudden burst of /token/refresh, per-token quota misattribution, and uneven token bucket refill leading to many quick 429->retry->503 paths.
root_cause: A combination of three factors: 1) a regression in the quota-enforcer that disabled per-token reservation during stubbed auth refresh paths; 2) no circuit-breaker on auth backend calls so retries compounded load; 3) the gateway's request prioritization logic treated auth refreshes as high-priority, starving normal request queues. The regression was introduced in runtime-1.26 when a refactor merged two quota maps and overlooked token-namespace collisions.
timeline: 2026-03-05T09:12Z: First spike detected by synthetic probe alert (elevated 5xx rate)
2026-03-05T09:16Z: Investigation: burst source identified as mobile token refresh pattern from a client release
2026-03-05T09:20Z: Mitigation: rate-limit rule applied at ingress to throttle /token/refresh to 50rps
2026-03-05T09:23Z: Partial recovery observed; 5xx rate dropped but some backlogged requests timed out
2026-03-05T09:29Z: Hotfix deployed to re-enable per-token reservation in quota-enforcer; rollout to 50% capacity
2026-03-05T09:34Z: Hotfix fully rolled out; metrics show stable token accounting and reduced 503s
mitigation: Ingress temporary throttling for /token/refresh to 50rps applied at edge (roll back after stabilizing)
Immediate rollback of the quota-enforcer merge in runtime-1.26 to restore per-token reservations
Increased timeouts and retry caps on client-facing downstream calls to avoid tight retry loops
postmortem_summary: This incident was triggered by an auth-token refresh storm exposing a hidden regression in quota accounting. The lack of backpressure and absence of a short-circuit for high-frequency auth refreshes allowed retries to amplify load, causing downstream 503s. The team deployed a targeted rollback and short-term ingress throttle which stabilized traffic. Root cause is a merge that collapsed token namespaces in the enforcer; the fix requires a code change, additional tests, and operational controls to prevent recurrence.
action_items: ENG: Add per-token reservation unit tests and fuzzing for token-namespace collisions (owner: Marco Alvarez, due: 2026-03-17)
